_comment: THE COMMITTED INDEX RECORD, declared once. Package data, not consumer data.
Before this file the record shape existed in four places and agreed with
itself only by habit: assembled inline twice in ingest/run.py (once for git
documents, once for url), policed by a DISPLAY_FIELDS tuple in
store/writer.py, carried forward by an EXTRACTED_FIELDS tuple in
ingest/run.py, and described in prose by SR-RECORD. Nothing compared them.
KEY ORDER HERE IS PRESENTATION ONLY. canonical_dumps sorts keys, so the
order in this file cannot reach a committed byte. What CAN reach one is the
field set, the defaults and omit_when -- which is why `schema` below must
match store/format.py's SCHEMA_ID: two fux versions with different shapes
must never both call their output fux.index.v4.
omit_when: a field equal to this value is LEFT OUT of the record rather
than written as false. That is SR-ARCHIVED-CONTENT decision 1 -- a live
record's shape is unchanged, so no existing consumer's parse breaks.
display: true marks text a human can read. L5 forbade these on a hashed
record; since W-194 (2026-09-20) there is no hashed record and no rule
reads this flag. It is kept as the one place that says which fields are
human-readable, so a future rule finds it instead of inventing a list.
carried: true marks a pure function of bytes that have not changed, so a
delta ingest may reuse the prior value instead of re-extracting. `edges` is
deliberately NOT carried: it is the one field the rest of the corpus can
change without this document changing.
EDGES, W-168 step 1 (2026-09-15, _format v3). Each entry is an object:
{kind, dst, grade}, and a `ref` edge also carries `at` (anchor term hash
-> count, from the LINK TEXT this document wrote) and `al` (the token
total, == sum of at's values; derive/_build.py asserts it). The words ride
the SOURCE document's edge, never the target's record -- that is the whole
of Arpit's 2026-09-15 ruling, option (c). An `anchor` field on the TARGET,
built from what everyone else calls it, would make a committed
per-document byte a function of other documents; editing B would move A's
bytes while the dirty list marked only B, and a full ingest and an
incremental re-index would produce different indexes from the same
sources. Terms, not text: link text is content, and L2 keeps content out
of the index.
_examples_doc: Two, one per source kind -- and since W-194 (2026-09-20) they differ only
in `src`, `loc` and the shape of the id. THE PRIVACY FORK IS GONE: `meta`
and `title_h` are deleted, law L5 is retired, and a url record carries a
plain `title` and `phrases` exactly as a git record does.
The leak L5 closed is ACCEPTED, not solved: a title alone tells a reader
that a document they cannot open exists. records/0007_LAW-5-hashed-meta.md
keeps the argument and the reopen trigger.
Both are shown as the DICT, not the committed line. The committed line is
`canonical_dumps` of this -- sorted keys, no spaces, one trailing newline.

url._note: Since W-194 a url record is shaped exactly like a git one.
url.title: Engineering handbook

_absent_from_the_examples_on_purpose: `archived: false` and `superseded: false` appear in NEITHER example, and
that is the point of `omit_when`: absent, not false. A live record's shape
stays unchanged, so no existing consumer's parse breaks. The git example
omits both; the url example carries `archived: true` because it is true.
`meta` and `title_h` are absent from BOTH examples because they no longer
exist (W-194). A v3 index carrying them is refused by `store/reader.py`
with a rebuild instruction rather than read and silently half-understood.
